newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Ekran says could change Bakun contractor.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Ekran says could change Bakun contractor.

text.p: Malaysia's Ekran Bhd said on Friday it could withdraw a $5.5 billion contract from Asea Brown Boveri for the construction of the giant Bakun hydroelectric project, local newspapers said on Thursday.

They quoted Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing as saying that if the ABB-led consortium did not agree with Ekran's view over the terms of the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract, it could be awarded to someone else.
"However, if ABB does not agree, somebody else will do the job...there are many other parties interested to do the job," he was quoted as telling reporters in the northern resort island of Langkawi.
He clarified that the situation had not reached a stage where a change of contractor needed to be considered.
Ekran, who was awarded the Bakun hydroelectric dam project in Sarawak state on Borneo island, has given the EPC contract to ABB and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO).
The dispute between Ekran and ABB, which is threatening to delay the $6.18 billion Bakun dam project, was over cost overruns, Ting said.
He said Ekran disagreed with terms in the contract that allowed the ABB-led consortium to claim cost overruns.

"We cannot have them (ABB consortium) claim any cost overruns as the EPC contract is a lump sum one. Any additional costs claimed will reduce the investment rate of return for shareholders," he told reporters at the third Langkawi International Dialogue conference.
Ting said this aspect had been overlooked in the EPC contract because it was negotiated when he was recuperating from a mild stroke.
Ting was quoted as saying that several meetings had been held between the ABB consortium and Bakun Hydro-Electric Corporation Bhd, the operator of the dam, but the differences remain.
"Yes, there has been a delay in the project, but I think it can still be completed on time," he said in reply to questions.
The project to generate 2,400 MW of power is scheduled for completion in 2003.
